title: Variational origin and Hausdorff-dimension prediction of $G_q$
html:
Remark. Variational origin and Hausdorff-dimension prediction of G_q

The gravitational constant G_q is derived from the categorical structure of the q-Yang--Mills--Levi action, not from semiclassical entropy-area relations. The key ingredient is the in-progress braid content of a Planck cell — the sections of the jet tower that are partially evaluated but not yet resolved to observable knots. This remark records the variational origin, the in-progress-braid counting, the quadratic suppression that produces S_{\mathrm{cell}}, and the numerical values at q_0. The associated Julia-set Hausdorff-dimension prediction is recorded separately (Hausdorff-dimension prediction).

The variational origin of G. The field equation \mathrm{Ric}_{g_\varTheta} = T^{(q)} (GR substrate geometry) arises from varying the q-Yang--Mills--Levi functional (q-YM-Levi)

  \mathfrak{S}_q[A, \varTheta]
  =  \int_M q(p)\lVert F_A^+|_H \rVert^2
  \varTheta \wedge (d\varTheta)^n

with respect to the Levi form L_\varTheta. The gravitational coupling G is the normalisation of this variation: it sets the ratio of curvature (\mathrm{Ric}_{g_\varTheta}) to stress-energy (T^{(q)}). In standard GR, this normalisation is postulated. In the QOU, it is determined by the information content of the brane tower at each fibre.

In-progress braids: sections that gravitate. At any fibre over a point p \in M, the jet tower A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow \cdots (jet-Planck steps) carries sections at every level. In one Planck time, n_R(q) \approx 10 jet prolongations complete. But the tower does not stop at level n_R: braids with crossing number c > n_R are partially evaluated.

A proton (c \sim 18 for its Borromean linking) at jet level 10 is an in-progress section — its braid word \beta \in B_n has been partially resolved (10 of \sim 18 R-matrix evaluations complete) but not yet descended to an observable knot. These in-progress braids are real sections of J^k\mathcal{S} over p: they carry partial crossing energy, they couple to the q-connection, and they contribute to T^{(q)}.

This is the categorical analog of virtual particles: the vacuum at p is populated by all braids "in transit" through the jet tower, each contributing to the gravitational source term.

Counting in-progress braids. At jet level k over a point p, the number of distinct in-progress braids is the dimension of the section space \Gamma(J^k\mathcal{S}|_p). For the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) Frobenius--Hopf object, this grows with k: each jet prolongation adds new polynomial coefficients (new Taylor data of the energy function E).

The total information content of a Planck cell is not the single-operation entropy \eta_q but the cumulative jet tower entropy:

  S_{\mathrm{cell}}(q)
  =  \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
  \eta_q^{(k)},

where \eta_q^{(k)} is the entropy contributed by sections at jet level k. The sum converges because sections at level k are exponentially suppressed by the descent involution \hat{\tau}_k (descent eigenspaces): the transient component at each level has support localised to exceptional divisors of codimension \geq 2.

Quadratic suppression from surface area. The exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_c \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) is a 2-sphere. Each jet level k adds a shell of in-progress braids whose information surface area scales as \hbar_q^2 (the square of the linear Reeb dimension), not \hbar_q. This is the holographic content of the descent involution: information on the exceptional divisor lives on 2-surfaces, and area is quadratic in the linear scale.

Concretely, the entropy at jet level k is suppressed by the area of the transient shell, not its radius:

  \eta_q^{(k)}
  =  \eta_q \cdot \hbar_q^{2k},

where the exponent 2k reflects that the codimension-2 localisation of transient sections (descent eigenspaces) projects onto a surface, and the surface area at level k scales as the square of the displacement \hbar_q^k. Summing the geometric series:

  S_{\mathrm{cell}}(q)
  =  \eta_q \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \hbar_q^{2k}
  =  \frac{\eta_q \cdot \hbar_q^2}{1 - \hbar_q^2}.

Exact algebraic closure. With the corrected operational entropy \eta_q = (2q-1)/q^3 (operational entropy) and 1 - \hbar_q^2 = (2q-1)/q^2, the series evaluates to

  S_{\mathrm{cell}}
  =  \frac{(2q-1)/q^3 \cdot (q-1)^2/q^2}{(2q-1)/q^2}
  =  \frac{(q-1)^2}{q^3}.

This is exactly the value required for G_{\mathrm{Planck}} = 1. No numerical fitting, no measured d_H input — the series closes algebraically from q alone.

The gravitational constant. The q-Yang--Mills--Levi variation gives

  G_q =  \frac{c_q^3 \cdot \hbar_q}{S_{\mathrm{cell}}(q)}
  =  \frac{c_q^3 \cdot \hbar_q \cdot (1 - \hbar_q^2)}
             {\eta_q \cdot \hbar_q^2}
  =  \frac{c_q^3 \cdot (2q - 1)}{q^2 \cdot \eta_q \cdot \hbar_q},

where c_q = 1/(q-1) is the speed of light (speed of light) and \hbar_q = (q-1)/q. Converting to Planck units:

  G_{\mathrm{Planck}}
  =  G_q \cdot \left(\frac{\hbar_q}{c_q}\right)^2
  =  1

identically for all q > 1.

Quadratic versus linear suppression. The \hbar_q^{2k} (not \hbar_q^k) exponent has a direct geometric origin: the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_c \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) \cong S^2 is a surface. Information on S^2 is proportional to area, and area is the square of the linear dimension. Each descent from level k+1 to level k projects out a codimension-2 shell whose area is \hbar_q^2 times the previous level. The linear suppression \hbar_q^k would correspond to information on a line (codimension 1) --- but the transient sections are localised to exceptional divisors of codimension \geq 2, giving the quadratic exponent.

This is the same reason that the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy scales as area (not volume): the information content of a region is determined by its boundary surface, and surfaces have area \sim r^2. In the QOU, this is not postulated but derived from the codimension-2 structure of the exceptional divisors in the brane tower.

Relation to the three fundamental constants.

The speed of light and Planck constant are algebraic in q. The gravitational constant requires the full jet tower information content — it is the only fundamental coupling that depends on the braid-group structure of the Frobenius--Hopf object, not just its ring-theoretic data. This explains why gravity is the hardest interaction to quantise and the weakest at low energies: its coupling is suppressed by the sparsity of in-progress braids (S_{\mathrm{cell}} \ll \eta_q) in the near-classical regime.
